summary: With the boundary question closed, I spent this turn on source-only work that answers the review question most likely to be asked next: whether the module's own expectations endorse the current classification, and whether anything in the snapshot would notice the gap. Reading the test files answers both, and the answer is sharper than expected. TestIsLocalMsg's expectation table (util_test.go:73-105) covers every message type in the enum except one — all 23 types from MsgHup (0) through MsgStorageApplyResp (22) — and the single type it omits is MsgForgetLeader, the last-numbered type at 23, so nothing in the table pins its classification either way and the table was simply never extended to the newest type. The two tests that drive the inbound path for every message type — TestRawNodeStep (rawnode_test.go:78-104) on RawNode.Step and TestNodeStep (node_test.go:51-84) on the public node.Step — both compute their expectation by calling IsLocalMsg on the very type under test, so a type absent from the table generates no assertion at all: the gap is structurally invisible to them, and classifying the type as local would break neither test. Along the way I confirmed the mechanism the earlier knowledge entry describes: the public node.Step silently returns nil for local types (unlike RawNode.Step, which returns ErrStepLocalMsg), while the internal node.step path that node.ForgetLeader uses pushes straight onto recvc and never passes through that filter, so both intended producers keep working under either classification. I deliberately did not inflate this into a finding: it does not by itself prove intent, so it is recorded as one fact entry in the index, with the two test files added as test_expectation sources and one sentence appended to the parent account's rationale (the only changes to that interpretation are source_ids and rationale; conclusion, defect_claim, executions, counterevidence and limitations are untouched and verified byte-identical). No experiment was filed, so nothing is left uncited, and the update validates with execution_requested=false.
